name: Activity Timeline
why: The catalog is 38,160 URLQuery reports, each a single timestamped row, and almost all activity falls in bursts from April to June 2026 aimed at a few data sources (UNCTAD alone is 19,319 of the 37,649 included reports). A timeline with one lane per data source lets the analyst see when each source was hit, how bursts from different sources overlap, and where the stronger ("significant") evidence sits, which the flat CSV hides.
arrangement:
Unit: One report, keyed by report_id (38,160 in all-reports.csv). report-sources.csv gives the data_source for the 37,649 included reports (join on report_id); the 432 review_required and 79 background reports have no source row and go in their own lanes named "Review required" and "Background control".
Overview: A horizontal time axis from 2025-11-01 to 2026-09-21 (report_date_utc, UTC), with a toggle to show the full range back to 2023-09 for the few early reports. One lane per data_source (40 display values, sorted by report count, largest first: UNCTAD, Thrill Data, AIHW, Woodlands House School, Mapillary, GBBC, ...), plus the two non-included lanes. Each lane shows reports per day as a bar or density strip, stacked or coloured by confidence (significant, suggestive, blank). A count of reports per lane at the lane's left.
Zoom: Brush or scroll to zoom the time axis from months to days to hours to minutes. At the hour or minute scale, each report becomes its own mark at its exact second, so bursts of many reports in the same minute are visible. Clicking a lane name isolates that lane.
Filter: Labels are the main filter. Also filter by disposition (included, review_required, background), confidence (significant, suggestive, blank), broad_class (source_request, indirection, custom_program), source_basis from report-sources.csv, and data_source. Whether the report is in the supplemental catalog (its report_id is in additional-cited-reports.csv) should be a selectable field too.
Details: Clicking a report shows its report_id, report_date_utc, disposition, confidence, broad_class, the full why_included text, source_basis and matched_sources, and a link to its report_url on urlquery.net (an outside page).
